item.title: Brain-computer interfaces in China: 12 companies, money and data
item.description: China approved the first implantable BCI, lets hospitals run implant studies on their own and raised over $1B in six months. 12 companies, their money and data.

item.title: A whole-brain interface from 70 patients: the Precision Neuroscience atlas
item.description: Precision recorded 70 patients with 1024-electrode surface grids and built an atlas of cortex, brainstem and spinal cord. What they found, and what I would train on this data.

item.title: Masked autoencoders learn perception-relevant representations from resting-state V1
item.description: We pretrain an MAE on 14.6 hours of spontaneous activity from V1 of a blind patient with a Utah array, and decode from the response to stimulation whether the person sees a phosphene. Our AAAI-26 workshop paper.

item.title: The most tasty neuro papers of 2025
item.description: My personal, completely subjective list of the best neural decoding papers of 2025: invasive and noninvasive foundation models, neuro tools, and one paper from our lab.

item.title: AAAI-26: impressions and tasty papers
item.description: My first AI conference, in Singapore: posters beat talks, four motor decoding labs in Beijing alone, Tolias and Schrimpf on scaling models of the brain. Plus four neuro papers from the conference I liked.

item.title: 3rd place at LibriBrain, NeurIPS 2025
item.description: Speech detection from MEG, 91% F1-macro, 3rd place. What surprised us, what worked (normalization, conv + transformer, weight averaging) and what didn't (augmentations, MAE pretraining, synthetic data).

item.title: Smart stimulation patterns for visual prostheses
item.description: Visual prostheses still use the same fixed stimulation patterns. A review of four papers that move toward models of perception, patient feedback and closed loop.

item.title: Understanding generative models: diffusion and flow matching
item.description: How DDPM and flow matching work at a high level, with the training and sampling code. Flow matching is a straight line from noise to data and an ODE solver.

item.title: People with visual implants barely use them in real life
item.description: Interviews with 6 developers and 6 users of Argus II and Orion. Developers overrate the devices; users say they are inconvenient and almost useless day to day. What users actually want.

item.title: SfN 2024: a periodic autoencoder for LFP
item.description: How I made a poster for SfN 24 with the University of Utah: an autoencoder with periodic regularization that pulls sinusoid-like components out of LFP. And why I never went to Chicago.

item.title: Transformers for brain decoding: POYO, NDT2 and MtM
item.description: Three foundation models for spikes: how they train across sessions and animals, what they use as a token, and how they pretrain. Plus what I would try next.

item.title: FingerFlex: inferring finger trajectories from ECoG signals
item.description: Our preprint FingerFlex: a simple U-Net-like encoder-decoder on wavelet features of ECoG predicts finger movements, correlation up to 0.74 on BCI Competition IV.
